question.text: What is the payoff of a long put option at expiry?

answer.text: max(K - S, 0) - Premium paid. Profit potential is substantial (up to K - Premium if the underlying falls to zero)
S - K if S > K; otherwise zero
Always equal to the premium received
K - S regardless of whether K > S or K < S

explanation.text: The Logic: A long put pays the positive difference between the strike and the closing index level. Net profit subtracts the premium paid. Breakeven is X - P. Maximum loss equals the premium paid, and maximum profit occurs if the underlying falls to zero (X - P per unit). The Trap: S - K is the call payoff, not the put payoff. The premium is paid by the buyer, not received. Note: USDINR calls hedge importers (dollar payables), while USDINR puts fit exporter or receivable exposure.
